name: Phu Quoc
tagline: Vietnam's largest island: white-sand beaches, warm calm water, fish-sauce factories, pepper farms and a jungle-covered interior, only a short hop from Saigon.
highlight: Swimming off Sao Beach in calm turquoise water, then dinner at the Duong Dong night market.
shortDescription: A tropical island in the Gulf of Thailand with long beaches, snorkelling, a national park, pepper and fish-sauce farms, night markets and a cable car to the offshore islands.
metaDescription: A Phu Quoc travel guide: Sao Beach, Long Beach, Duong Dong night market, Hon Thom cable car, pepper farms, fish sauce, snorkelling, best time, how to get there and a four-day plan.
nearestAirport: Phu Quoc International (PQC), about 10 minutes from Duong Dong
knownFor: Beaches, seafood, fish sauce, snorkelling, sunsets

image.alt: The sun setting over the sea at a beach on Phu Quoc island

intro: Phu Quoc is Vietnam's largest island, about 45 km long, lying in the Gulf of Thailand, closer to Cambodia than to the Vietnamese mainland. Its interior is covered with forest, much of it a national park, and its western coast has long sandy beaches facing the sunset. For decades it was a quiet place of fishing villages and plantations, and it has become the country's leading beach resort, with big resorts, a new international airport and a growing list of attractions.

The island is still known for its traditional industries. Its fish sauce, made by fermenting anchovies in large wooden barrels, is prized across Vietnam and protected by an EU geographical indication. Black pepper farms, pearl farms and a local breed of dog, the Phu Quoc ridgeback, are other symbols. Night markets in Duong Dong sell seafood, and the south of the island has fishing communities and offshore islands.

Development has been rapid, and some of the best-known beaches now have resorts and traffic, but there are still quieter corners, particularly in the north and the south-east. It is a good place for a few days of rest at the end of a Vietnam trip, particularly in the dry season.

whyVisit.intro: Phu Quoc is the easiest place in Vietnam for a beach holiday, with a mix of resorts and rustic corners.

points.title: Beautiful beaches
points.text: Sao Beach, Long Beach, Ong Lang and others offer fine sand and calm water.

points.title: Snorkelling and boat trips
points.text: The An Thoi islands in the south have coral reefs and clear water.

points.title: Seafood and night markets
points.text: Fresh fish, squid and crab at low prices.

points.title: Local products
points.text: Fish sauce, pepper, pearls and honey.

points.title: Nature
points.text: A national park with forest trails and waterfalls.

attractionsIntro: The island is spread out, and the sights are best combined by area.

attractions.name: Sao Beach

image.alt: White sand and turquoise water at Sao Beach on Phu Quoc

attractions.text: The island's most beautiful beach, on the south-east coast, with soft white sand and calm, clear water.
attractions.tip: Go on a weekday, and arrive early.

attractions.name: Long Beach and Duong Dong
attractions.text: A long strip of sand on the west coast, with resorts, restaurants and the main town, and the Dinh Cau night market.

attractions.name: Dinh Cau Night Market

image.alt: Stalls at the Dinh Cau Night Market in Duong Dong, Phu Quoc

attractions.text: A nightly market with seafood stalls, souvenirs and local snacks, beside the Dinh Cau temple.

attractions.name: Hon Thom Cable Car

image.file: File:Hon Thom Cable Car aerial view Phu Quoc Island Vietnam.jpg
image.alt: The Hon Thom cable car crossing the sea from Phu Quoc

attractions.text: One of the longest sea-crossing cable cars in the world, from An Thoi to Hon Thom island, with a water park and views.

attractions.name: The southern islands
attractions.text: The An Thoi archipelago, with snorkelling and diving among coral reefs, reached by boat tours.
attractions.tip: Book a tour with a good operator.

attractions.name: Fish sauce factories and pepper farms
attractions.text: Visit the barrels of fermenting fish sauce and the peppercorn plantations in the north.

thingsToDoIntro: Phu Quoc is for the beach first, and for day trips second.

thingsToDo.title: Snorkel or dive
thingsToDo.text: Coral reefs and clear water off the An Thoi islands.

thingsToDo.title: Eat seafood at the night market
Watch the sunset
thingsToDo.text: The west coast is ideal, with beach bars and restaurants.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring a jacket for the breeze.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a fish sauce factory
thingsToDo.text: See how the sauce is made, and taste it.
thingsToDo.tip: Buy a bottle to take home.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the national park
thingsToDo.text: Forest trails, waterfalls and viewpoints in the north.

thingsToDo.title: Take a squid-fishing trip
thingsToDo.text: An evening trip to fish for squid with lights.

foodIntro: Phu Quoc's food is seafood and fish sauce, with a range of local specialities.

foods.name: Grilled seafood
foods.text: Squid, crab, prawns, scallops and fish, cooked to order.
foods.whereToTry: The night market and beach restaurants.

foods.name: Bun quay
foods.text: Fresh noodles in a broth with fish, a Phu Quoc speciality.

foods.name: Herring salad (goi ca trich)
foods.text: Raw herring with coconut, herbs and peanuts.

foods.name: Sea urchin and sea snails
foods.text: Fresh shellfish grilled with spring onions.

foods.name: Sim wine and pepper
foods.text: Wine made from rose myrtle, and local black pepper.

accommodation.intro: Choose the coast that suits you. The west has the most choice, and the south-east is quieter.

areas.name: Long Beach
areas.text: Hotels, resorts and beach bars, near Duong Dong.

gettingThere.intro: Phu Quoc is reached by air, or by ferry from the mainland.

options.text: Direct flights from Ho Chi Minh City (about 1 hour), Hanoi and other cities, and some international routes.
options.detail: The airport is close to Duong Dong.

options.mode: Ferry from Rach Gia or Ha Tien
options.text: About 2 to 3 hours by ferry from mainland ports in the Mekong Delta.
Via Ha Tien, near the Cambodian border, and then by ferry.

gettingAround.intro: The island is large, and a scooter or taxi is needed.

options.text: The most popular way to explore.
options.detail: Wear a helmet, and check insurance.

options.text: Most resorts arrange transfers and day trips.

bestTime.headline: November–April
bestTime.summary: Phu Quoc has a tropical climate, with a dry season from November to April and a wet season with rough seas from May to October.

seasons.text: Sunny, dry, calm seas and clear water.
Hot and dry, with warm seas.
Heavy rain, rougher seas and some closures. Green and cheap.

bestTime.avoid: August to October, the wettest months, when the sea is rough and murky.

itinerary.title: Four days in Phu Quoc
itinerary.intro: Beach days with a mix of tours and markets.

days.title: The south
days.afternoon: Snorkelling in the An Thoi islands.

days.title: The north
days.morning: A pepper farm and fish sauce factory.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you plan the island.
tips: Visit in the dry season, from November to April.
Rent a scooter only if you have experience, a licence and insurance.
Choose the beach area carefully, as they differ a lot.
Check prices at seafood stalls before ordering.
Book snorkelling tours with reputable operators.
Buy fish sauce and pepper from producers.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Phu Quoc?
faq.a: Three or four days for beaches and the main attractions.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: November to April. The wet season has rougher seas.
Sao Beach for beauty, Long Beach for services, and Ong Lang for quiet.
Yes, for a beach break, though it is more developed than it used to be.

faq.q: Can I visit from Ho Chi Minh City?
faq.a: Yes, about one hour by air.

faq.q: Is it safe to ride a scooter?
faq.a: Roads are quiet outside the main areas, but accidents are common. Take care and wear a helmet.
